notes:
Fragments from calls + internal CRM notes:
- Primary pain: seasonal and event-driven spikes (product launches + holidays) create queue backpressure, long hold times, and tool rate-limit failures.
- Target metrics quoted by Ops: p95 latency for agent-assist < 250ms during normal ops, p95 < 650ms acceptable during sustained spikes; ticket summarization p95 < 1s.
- Throughput profile: baseline ~10k req/min for agent assist, common bursts to 30-50k req/min for 5-30 minutes, rare sustained peaks 1-3 hours during promos.
- Use-case details: agent-assist (real-time snippets, next-best-action), tool-calling (CRM writebacks + ticket routing), ticket_summarization (batch after shift), and automated reranking for prioritization.
- "We can't have dropped writes to our CRM — must be exactly-once or strong retry guarantees" — Head of Integrations.
- Interested in Dedicated pools with pre-warm and autoscale bumping; evaluating Redwood's warm pool behavior and cold-start cost during bursts.
- Security: strict EU residency for a chunk of customers; SOC2 + SSO/SAML + audit logs required. Legal flagged data retention controls.
- Cost sensitivity: CFO wants unit-cost delta between hosted vs dedicated vs private at 50k rps spikes; willing to pay for reliability but needs predictable commit.
- POC scope agreed: three simulated profiles (short burst, long sustained, holiday surge) with log collection (latency/tail, error taxonomy), and a canary fallback to cheaper model variant to preserve throughput when ideal model is saturated.
- SE notes: test with quantized model variant for fallback, verify KV/prefix caching for multi-turn agent dialogs, measure per-token cost under batching.
- Current blockers: legal questions on EU on-prem options (drive doc linked), finance needs spreadsheet for peak-hour ARR impact, and security wants KMS/HSM integration detail.
- Next steps: POC run, deliver final cost model and SLA mapping, security sign-off.
